key_insight: Real patient-chatbot interactions are highly diverse, and that diversity can materially change how LLMs assess urgency.
clinical_relevance: Triage and symptom-assessment chatbots may perform well in idealized tests but underperform or misclassify risk when users communicate with real-world variation in emotion, style, and strategy.
method: Analyzed 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations to characterize communication diversity.
Built a patient simulator that models clinical content, emotion, conversational strategy, and communication style separately.
Tested four LLMs across five patient personae in 1,164 clinician-graded cases and evaluated simulator realism with human graders.
evidence_signal: In a Turing-inspired realism test with 15 human graders, simulated conversations were nearly indistinguishable from real ones, with 55% accuracy overall.
watch_item: Results suggest a risk of biased or unstable triage performance if systems are developed and validated only on cooperative, articulate, idealized patient interactions.
paper_title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
